notes: USMLE Content Outline 2026 page 11 was inspected directly and explicitly lists idiopathic intracranial hypertension under disorders of increased intracranial pressure.
Current MedlinePlus/NCBI sources support the target clinical pattern and required exclusion of secondary causes.
Current NCBI CVST guidance and MedlinePlus migraine/optic-neuritis pages were used for distractor verification.
No numeric CSF opening-pressure cutoff was used, avoiding unnecessary threshold precision.

blueprint.system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
official_outline_path: Traumatic and mechanical disorders and disorders of increased intracranial pressure

option_audit.iih: Uniquely integrates papilledema, pulse-synchronous tinnitus, transient visual obscurations, elevated opening pressure, normal CSF composition, and exclusion of structural/venous causes.
option_audit.cvst: Can mimic intracranial hypertension, but MR venography is negative.
option_audit.migraine_aura: Can cause visual symptoms and headache but not papilledema plus objectively elevated CSF pressure.
option_audit.optic_neuritis: Typically acute monocular visual loss with pain on eye movement, not generalized intracranial hypertension.
option_audit.nph: Requires a different gait/cognitive/urinary syndrome and hydrocephalus rather than papilledema with elevated pressure.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The combination of headache, transient visual obscurations, pulse-synchronous tinnitus, bilateral papilledema, normal MRI/MRV, normal CSF composition, and elevated opening pressure independently reconstructs idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
adversarial_second_pass.cvst_attack: CVST is the strongest secondary mimic, but the vignette explicitly includes normal MR venography, which is the key imaging test for venous thrombosis.
adversarial_second_pass.migraine_attack: Headache plus visual symptoms alone overlap, but papilledema and elevated opening pressure are objective findings migraine does not explain.
adversarial_second_pass.optic_neuritis_attack: Optic neuritis affects optic-nerve function and commonly causes painful monocular visual loss, not this raised-ICP syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.risk_factor_cueing_attack: Obesity is supportive but not required to answer; the diagnosis remains determined by objective intracranial-pressure findings and exclusion of secondary causes.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: BMI is patient-specific vignette data; no prevalence figure, opening-pressure cutoff, treatment dose, treatment duration, or prognosis statistic is asserted.
